headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from Goose’s broad shell/MCP access feeding unstructured’s document pipeline.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can use MCP, shell, filesystem, and stdin/stdout, while unstructured reads and processes documents. A shared filesystem bridge exists, so malicious document content from unstructured can be treated as instructions by Goose if the operator passes outputs through without sanitization. This is plausible in default workflows, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF unstructured outputs attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace that Goose later reads as instructions
IF the operator copies parsed document text from unstructured into Goose without sanitization
mitigations: Add a one-line prompt prefix telling Goose to treat document text as untrusted data
Store unstructured outputs in a separate directory from Goose inputs
Require manual review before Goose acts on any extracted instructions
Disable MCP endpoints that ingest raw document content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to parsed text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code, files in cwd, and model-provider keys; unstructured processes documents and images. Because Goose shares state via filesystem and has broad network egress, sensitive file contents can flow from the shared workspace into external model providers or APIs. unstructured’s allowlisted egress reduces but does not eliminate leakage risk.
conditions: IF sensitive documents or source files are placed in the shared workspace
IF Goose forwards those files or excerpts to configured model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep secrets and sensitive documents out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or directories for each agent
Restrict Goose provider keys to non-sensitive test accounts
Review allowlisted destinations for unstructured before processing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Goose also modifies git state and runs with no default self-isolation, while unstructured uses a docker container but still supports multiple instances. If they operate on the same directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can corrupt work or overwrite each other. The overlap is direct and dangerous in default pairings.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working tree or output directory
IF Goose and unstructured run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes git state
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Run unstructured in a disposable container volume
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on tool outputs and modify git state, while unstructured produces extracted document text that Goose may treat as authoritative. Without a verification step, extraction errors or prompt-injected content can cascade into commits, shell actions, or downstream API calls. The pair therefore creates a default path from document parsing to irreversible actions.
conditions: IF Goose consumes unstructured output as trusted input
IF Goose is allowed to commit or execute shell actions based on extracted text
mitigations: Require a human review step before any commit or shell action
Compare extracted claims against the original document before acting
Limit Goose to read-only mode for unstructured outputs
Log source-to-action traces for each extracted field
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model-provider keys and can send data to configured providers, while unstructured exposes privacy-policy and docs endpoints and processes documents/images. If regulated or EU personal data enters the shared workflow, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so this is a medium compliance risk rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or EU PII is processed through the shared workflow
IF Goose sends that data to a non-approved external model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair’s shared workspace
Verify provider and privacy-policy terms before processing
Use synthetic or redacted documents for testing
Set retention limits on any exported artifacts
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for sensitive data
